title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
subtitle: spicy glazed wings with a tangy sauce
excerpt: Crispy baked chicken wings tossed in a buttery hot sauce. They are baked rather than deep-fried, which keeps things simple without losing the crunch. Serve with soured cream for dipping.
sourceNotes: Buffalo wings were invented at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, in 1964. The original sauce is butter and hot sauce. They quickly became a fixture at American bars and sports events.

content.text: Pat the wings completely dry before baking. Moisture is the enemy of crispiness. A high oven temperature gives you that crunchy exterior without deep frying.

items.prepNote: use a few dashes of hot sauce

content.text: Preheat oven to 220C (fan 200C / gas 7). Pat the wings very dry with kitchen paper.
Toss the wings with flour, cayenne, and salt in a bowl. Spread on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, turning halfway, until very crispy and golden.
While wings bake, melt the butter in a small pan. Add hot sauce, vinegar, and honey. Stir and simmer for 2 minutes.
Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve immediately.

items.cause: Wings were wet or oven not hot enough
items.fix: Dry the wings well and use the highest oven setting. A wire rack on the baking sheet also helps air circulate underneath.
Simmer the sauce for a few extra minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.

items.cause: Oven too hot or wings too small
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil after 25 minutes if colouring too fast. The inside needs to reach 75C.

content.text: Buffalo wings were created at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York in 1964. Teressa Bellissimo reportedly tossed leftover wings in hot sauce and butter as a late-night snack for her son and his friends. The dish spread rapidly across America through the 1970s and 1980s. Today buffalo wings are one of the most eaten bar snacks in the United States.
